title: Ramakrishna (the Gospel, selections)
hook: a doll made of salt walks into the sea to measure how deep it is

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ramakrishna's snake, told to stop biting, and the holy man's line: I never told you not to hiss. A hiss is not a bite.

A doll made entirely of salt sets out to measure the ocean. Small doll, big job: find out how deep the water goes, then come back and report. It walks down to the shore and steps in. And right there the story stops being about measuring, because the moment the doll is in the water, it starts to dissolve. Ramakrishna told this little parable when people asked him a question that sounds simple: what is God like, really?
screen: `A DOLL MADE OF SALT.` → `IT GOES TO MEASURE THE OCEAN.` → `IT NEVER COMES BACK.`

segments.voice: His visitors were often educated men, used to debating. They wanted a definition. He gave them pictures instead, and the Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna, the book of his conversations, is full of them. The salt doll went to measure the ocean, and it melted. So who was left to come back and say how deep it was? That is his answer about Brahman, the reality the Upanishads point to beyond every name. You can't stand outside it and take its measurements, because the one measuring is made of the same stuff. Get close enough, and the measurer is gone. He makes the same point another way, and it's startling. Everything, he says, has become uchchhishta, food that has already been tasted: leftovers. The Vedas, the scriptures, the philosophies have all passed through human mouths. Only Brahman has never been made leftover, because no one has ever been able to say what it is. Notice what he isn't saying. He isn't throwing scripture away. He sang hymns, quoted the sacred books, and worshiped the Mother in the temple. Words point, and what they point to is bigger than any mouth. And the parable isn't a sad one. The doll goes in because it wants to know. Some readers add that a doll of salt came from the sea in the first place. Its not coming back is the answer.
screen: `THE SALT DOLL MELTS.` · `NO ONE COMES BACK TO REPORT.` · `EVERYTHING ELSE IS LEFTOVERS.` · `WORDS POINT; THEY DON'T CONTAIN.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind something you love that you've never managed to explain well: a person, a place, a piece of music, or, if you pray, God. Try silently to describe it in one sentence, and notice how the sentence falls short. Then let the sentence go, and simply stay near the thing itself, the way the doll stood at the water's edge.
Ramakrishna. The temple priest at Dakshineswar who answered hard questions with small pictures. Today's picture: the salt doll that went to measure the ocean.
Your line: the measurer is gone. Tomorrow, a lizard that won't stay one color. Rest well.

howItsDone: Devotees read the Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna in study circles and at centers of the Ramakrishna order, and his parables, like the salt doll, are retold in talks and at home.

fork.setup: you're the salt doll, standing at the edge of the sea with a job: measure how deep it goes. what happens?
options: you wade in, measure, and come back.
you step in, and dissolve into the water.
you measure from the shore and guess.
fork.reveal: the doll melts the moment it enters. for Ramakrishna, that's the point: the one who goes to measure Brahman doesn't come back separate.

original.note: Sanskrit (used in Bengali too): food already tasted, leftovers. Ramakrishna said everything but Brahman has become this.

trapdoor: what you thought: a cute story about a doll at the beach.
what it means: you can't measure Brahman from outside, because the one measuring melts into it.
what a scholar hears: in the Gospel, the same teaching comes as uchchhishta: every scripture has been tasted by human mouths, and only Brahman has never been put into words.

chat.says: If Ramakrishna talked about God all day, why didn't he just define God?
options: He said you can't measure it from outside: like the salt doll, the measurer melts in.
He hadn't studied enough philosophy to try, so he told stories instead.
He kept the definition secret, for his closest disciples only.
chat.meaning: The salt doll melts as it measures. For Ramakrishna, only Brahman has never been made leftover, because no one can say what it is.
